brief.headline: Push for a 16.6% price cut on the PET bottle SKU to match our best price — we already pay ₹1.87/NOS elsewhere, and their finances are tight enough to make the deal worth it.

priceAsk.summary: Cut the PET BOT AMBER 100ML/25MM NECK 12.5G from ₹2.18/NOS to ₹1.87/NOS
priceAsk.target: ₹1.87/NOS — the best price we pay today, saving us ₹28644 a year
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹1.87/NOS to Suraj Blow Plast PVt. Ltd. for the same bottle. TPAC charges ₹2.18/NOS — a 16.6% gap. The market ask for a similar cap sits at ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc), with modest room to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume — so our ₹1.87/NOS target is grounded in what we pay and what the market supports.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move payment from 30 days to 45 days — offer to pay at 15 days instead in exchange for a ~10% price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Keeping 30 days frees up ₹93078 of cash for us. If we pay 15 days faster than today, we give up ₹46539 — worth it only if they cut price by roughly their borrowing rate of 10.27%.

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC brings in ₹637.48 Cr a year and keeps about ₹4 of every ₹100 they sell (3.8%). They borrow money at about 10.27%, and their cash is stuck for 79 days — the same as similar firms (79d peer median) but tighter than most because they pay suppliers in only 17 days versus a peer median of 33d. Their credit rating is [ICRA] A / Stable, so they're not about to collapse, but the Altman Z-score of 2.77 puts them in the grey zone — not distress, but not safe either — plus they've had GST filing delays and EPF payment delays. We're only 0.02% of their sales (₹11.32 L), so on our own we're too small to move them; bundle more SKUs, commit volume for a year, or play them against Manjushree or Pearl Polymers to get their attention.

evidence.point: We pay ₹2.18/NOS; our best price elsewhere is ₹1.87/NOS — a 16.6% gap
evidence.figure: Gap: 16.6%; bestPrice: ₹1.87/NOS (Suraj Blow Plast PVt. Ltd.); ourPrice: ₹2.18/NOS

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; the top second-source candidate and big enough to absorb our volume.

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle/jar specialist (Pearlpet) — a direct fit for our PET BOT AMBER 100ML bottle SKU.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader in pails, containers, pharma packaging — strong, profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

risks: At ₹11.32 L (0.02% of their sales) we're too small to matter alone — bundle more SKUs or commit a longer term to get leverage.
Their Altman Z of 2.77 is grey-zone and they've missed GST/EPF deadlines — push hard but watch that we don't tip a fragile supplier; qualify a second source now in case they stumble.
They pay suppliers in 17 days (peer median 33d) so their own cash is tight — a faster-payment offer will appeal, but don't give it away without a matching price cut of ~10%.

The market ask for a 28 mm cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95) with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume — our ₹1.87/NOS bottle target is grounded, but if they push back hard, cross-check the spec and MOQ before committing.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're paying you ₹2.18 a bottle when we pay Suraj ₹1.87 for the same thing — let's close that 16.6% gap and talk about how faster payment or a longer commit can sweeten the deal for both of us.
